steps.title: Choose explicit classroom limits
steps.explanation: Select depth, concurrency and estimated spend independently. This three-service teaching example uses smaller explicit caps rather than relying on runtime defaults.
steps.narration: Step 1. Select depth, concurrency and estimated spend independently. This three-service teaching example uses smaller explicit caps rather than relying on runtime defaults. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Build string-valued cap environment
steps.explanation: Pass depth and Agent concurrency through env strings. Workflow has a separate concurrency setting; a serial workflow uses one slot.
steps.narration: Step 2. Pass depth and Agent concurrency through env strings. Workflow has a separate concurrency setting; a serial workflow uses one slot. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Apply the native spend cap
steps.code:
maxBudgetUsd: limits.budgetUsd,
    effort: "low",
    thinking: { type: "disabled" },
    abortController: controller,
steps.explanation: maxBudgetUsd bounds estimated spend for the query and child requests. It is not a prepaid currency reservation; a request can cross the threshold before the SDK stops.
steps.narration: Step 3. maxBudgetUsd bounds estimated spend for the query and child requests. It is not a prepaid currency reservation; a request can cross the threshold before the SDK stops. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Preserve the launching environment
steps.code:
env: {
      ...process.env,
      HOME: w.home,
      USERPROFILE: w.home,
      CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: w.sdkHome,
      ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: undefined,
      CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY: "1",
      ...capEnvironment(c.mode),
    },
steps.explanation: TypeScript env replaces the subprocess environment. Spread process.env, keep private credentials on the server, isolate settings, and append the explicit caps.
steps.narration: Step 4. TypeScript env replaces the subprocess environment. Spread process.env, keep private credentials on the server, isolate settings, and append the explicit caps. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Define a coordinator that can request a grandchild
steps.code:
coordinator: {
      description:
        "Delegates one service review if depth permits, otherwise performs the read-only audit itself.",
      prompt:
        "Use Agent to delegate the supplied service file to auditor if Agent is available. If depth restrictions removed Agent, Read the file yourself and explicitly report that Agent is unavailable. Never invent delegation or modify files. Report under 50 words.",
      tools: ["Agent", "Read"],
      model: "inherit",
      maxTurns: 6,
steps.explanation: The coordinator declares Agent and Read. The runtime depth limit can remove Agent from the bottom layer; depth 1 and depth 2 produce different native trees.
steps.narration: Step 5. The coordinator declares Agent and Read. The runtime depth limit can remove Agent from the bottom layer; depth 1 and depth 2 produce different native trees. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Detect actual direct and nested Agent calls
steps.explanation: Retain all real Agent tool-use blocks, including nested delegations with a parent tool-use ID. A parent report alone does not prove a grandchild ran.
steps.narration: Step 6. Retain all real Agent tool-use blocks, including nested delegations with a parent tool-use ID. A parent report alone does not prove a grandchild ran. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Retain native tool refusal results
steps.explanation: Record actual tool-return content and is_error. Concurrency refusal is a native result, not a host-invented simulation, and refused services remain unaudited.
steps.narration: Step 7. Record actual tool-return content and is_error. Concurrency refusal is a native result, not a host-invented simulation, and refused services remain unaudited. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Handle the native budget result before the exception
steps.code:
status: message.subtype,
            text:
              message.subtype === "success"
                ? message.result
                : message.errors.join("\n"),
            costUsd: message.total_cost_usd,
            modelUsage: message.modelUsage,
          };
steps.explanation: Retain result subtype, errors and estimated cost even when the SDK then raises. Budget mode expects error_max_budget_usd rather than treating it as a successful audit.
steps.narration: Step 8. Retain result subtype, errors and estimated cost even when the SDK then raises. Budget mode expects error_max_budget_usd rather than treating it as a successful audit. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Scope file access independently
steps.explanation: Permit only the three disposable service files and classroom instructions. Reviewers and workflow agents cannot edit source, execute shell commands or inspect .env.
steps.narration: Step 9. Permit only the three disposable service files and classroom instructions. Reviewers and workflow agents cannot edit source, execute shell commands or inspect .env. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Launch the reviewed Workflow script
steps.explanation: The host supplies its fixed reviewed script through the native hook. Workflow is enabled in allowedTools, and repeat or unrelated launches are not approved.
steps.narration: Step 10. The host supplies its fixed reviewed script through the native hook. Workflow is enabled in allowedTools, and repeat or unrelated launches are not approved. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Declare native workflow metadata and inputs
steps.explanation: A Workflow script begins with literal metadata, then a phase and fixed service inputs. The runtime provides agent and pipeline globals outside the parent conversation.
steps.narration: Step 11. A Workflow script begins with literal metadata, then a phase and fixed service inputs. The runtime provides agent and pipeline globals outside the parent conversation. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Coordinate reviewers and return one result
steps.explanation: Use agent for each read-only audit, pipeline to fan out over the list and script variables to retain intermediate reports. Return the consolidated result after completion.
steps.narration: Step 12. Use agent for each read-only audit, pipeline to fan out over the list and script variables to retain intermediate reports. Return the consolidated result after completion. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.

steps.title: Independently verify fixture integrity
steps.code:
fixtureUnchanged: before.hash === after.hash,
      fixture: after,
      observations,
      exceptions,
      scaling: {
steps.explanation: Hash all three real service fixtures after the run. Native limits, observed child activity and unchanged files are separate pieces of evidence.
steps.narration: Step 13. Hash all three real service fixtures after the run. Native limits, observed child activity and unchanged files are separate pieces of evidence. This source excerpt shows the corresponding application statement.
